title: The sign-in request size limit is documented
lines: The API guide now says a sign-in request that must survive GitHub sign-in can be at most 2,000 characters.
Longer requests cannot be kept through GitHub sign-in.

title: Friendlier draft list and login
lines: Draft list buttons have plain labels: Duplicate, Delete draft and New draft.
Action buttons measure 44 pixels.
A visible ring shows which control has keyboard focus.
Screen readers announce status messages.

title: Sharing and preview look updated
lines: The Agent link button has a plain label.
Status tooltips are announced to screen readers and stay on screen at 390 pixels.
The export panel has one main action.
Controls are 44 pixels tall and have a visible focus ring.

title: Settings page layout changed
lines: Connected apps now sits below the page heading.
The deployment banner no longer appears on every page.
It is now one small About line at the bottom of Settings.

title: The code check covers the whole project
lines: The code check runs on the whole project.
Long functions were split into smaller ones, and the build step was moved out of the check.
It replaces an older change that was out of date.

title: Hardening plan shows finished work
lines: Each task's status line in the hardening plan now names its merged pull request.
Four tasks are parked for later.
The current plan points to the finished plan and the parked tasks.

title: Plan for connecting AI apps
lines: A written plan covers connecting Claude Code, Claude, Codex and ChatGPT to the app, in numbered steps.
A reminder prints the plan's rules at the start of each work session and after a summary of the chat.

title: Preview names and storage status recorded
lines: The stable preview has one name for its code branch and another for its database branch.
The storage step has no preview deployment, and the final record says it was not run.

title: Owner reporting rules are written down
lines: Every item is numbered, and owner questions are answered in one template table.
Decisions are recorded in the ledger.

title: Claude Code and Codex can now sign in
lines: Sign-in accepts a return address on any local port.
Sign-in no longer needs the extra resource setting that Codex leaves out.

title: Older AI apps can connect now
lines: A request with no version header is handled as the older protocol version, 2025-03-26, instead of being refused.
The log now records the other site when a request from it is refused.

title: AI apps get clearer tool details and links
lines: Every tool has a title and four hints that tell AI apps which actions need a confirmation.
Share links come with a preview link and a Markdown link.
Draft results include a link to the editor.

title: AI apps can show accounts and make threads
lines: AI apps can show the connected account, make a thread in one call, and remove an image.
Adding an image from a link can now name the post it goes to.
A test now fails when a route has no AI tool and is not skipped on purpose.

title: Image removal through AI apps fixed
lines: Removing an image now counts how many other drafts use it.
Only files owned by your account are deleted.
A successful removal no longer returns a forbidden error.

title: Edits made during an image upload are kept
lines: Adding an image from a link to a post keeps edits made while the upload runs.
The window in which this can go wrong is short, but it is not zero.

title: AI apps can change one post at a time
lines: AI apps can add, change, remove or move one post without resending the rest of the thread.
Published drafts cannot be changed this way.

title: AI apps can export numbered threads
lines: A draft can be exported as numbered text, the same as the numbered copy in the app.
The same numbered text is available through the API and the AI app tools.

title: Remote links cannot reach private addresses
lines: Metadata documents and remote images now connect only to the address that was checked.
If a site switches to a private address after the check, the app still does not connect to it.
Any host whose answer includes a private address is refused.
Redirects are still not followed.

title: AI apps are limited to 120 calls a minute
lines: Each user can make 120 tool calls a minute through AI apps.
A call over the limit gets a tool error, not a protocol error.
Records older than one day are cleared during the regular token cleanup.

title: A connector guide for AI apps
lines: A new guide covers tool groups, four setup recipes, what is not available, disconnecting and troubleshooting.
The four setup recipes have not yet been checked against current client docs.
The guide is linked from several pages, including the README and the API guide.
The public smoke check now covers three more sign-in details.

title: Settings lists four AI apps to connect
lines: Settings has a Connect an AI app section with Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT and Codex CLI.
Each entry has a copy button for the connector address or the exact command.
The page says each app needs approving once with GitHub sign-in.

title: The AI app connection plan is finished
lines: The plan is marked completed, and the session reminder no longer prints anything.
Four runs with real AI apps are still left for the owner to do.
The platform guide has a line about the Connect an AI app section in Settings.

title: A test now runs five AI app requests
lines: A new automated test sends the five checklist requests to the server.
It covers a one-time share link and a sign-in refresh before the last list.
It checks the server only, with no person. Runs with real AI apps stay with the owner.

title: Rules for end-to-end tests and owner steps
lines: A fixed model settles questions about end-to-end work.
An end-to-end test that needs a person is redesigned, not accepted.
Steps for the owner are written once, with exact steps and the reply that unblocks them.

title: A Claude Code sign-in test is added
lines: A test now signs Claude Code in through the app's connector, with no person involved.
It runs only through the clients test command, not before each commit.

title: The unused-code check allows one more tool
lines: The unused-code check now allows the script tool, which the sign-in test uses.
This fixes a failing unit test check.

title: Codex sign-in test waits for its prompt
lines: The Codex sign-in test waits for the Callback URL prompt before it sends the redirect.
Input sent too early could be dropped, which made the clients check time out.

title: Codex sign-in test fails on errors
lines: The Codex sign-in test now fails when Codex exits with an error.
It passes only when Codex prints "Successfully logged in".
The dev server and login process are always stopped, even on failure.

title: Claude Code sign-in test fails on errors
lines: The Claude Code sign-in test now fails when the tool exits with an error.
It passes only when the tool prints "Authenticated with x-thread".
The dev server and login process are always stopped, even on failure.

title: Codex sign-in test follows the redirect
lines: The Codex sign-in test now opens the approval redirect the way a browser does.
Pasting the redirect in did not finish sign-in during the clients check.
A failure now prints the end of Codex's output.

title: Tests no longer use real AI app logins
lines: Tests no longer use real AI apps or their accounts.
Each AI app setup is checked through the real server code, with no app, account or token.
The separate clients check script and its command were removed.

title: One post can change without resending the thread
lines: Changing one post's text now saves only that post.
A repeat of the same change writes nothing new.
If the draft changed since it was read, the change is refused.
If a save fails partway, its changes are undone.
Each draft keeps a version number that goes up with every change.

title: Sign-in refresh checks the resource
lines: A refresh request for a different resource is refused with an invalid target error.
The refusal does not use up the refresh token.
A refresh request with no resource still works.

title: A test checks the AI app sign-in flow
lines: A new test plays the part of an AI app through the whole sign-in and tool flow.
Each tool's input rules are checked strictly.
It needs no app, account, person or AI model, and refuses any other outside request.

title: A test can no longer commit to the repo
lines: The Vercel ignore test can no longer write commits into the project's repository.

title: A test uses the official MCP client
lines: A new test uses the official MCP client library to run the full sign-in and tool flow inside the app.
It makes no network calls and needs no app, person or AI model.

title: Draft saves now check for conflicts
lines: Saving or publishing a whole draft now happens as one step.
If the draft changed since it was read, the save is refused.
Repeating a save that already happened changes nothing.
AI apps can give a new post an ID of their own.
Repeating an add with the same ID writes nothing, and different text under that ID is refused.

title: The AI app plan shows every step done
lines: The AI app connection plan marks every step done, with the pull request for each step.
The current plan says all steps are merged.

title: Plan adds AI app prompts and wording
lines: The AI app plan has a new section on prompts, skills, Hebrew text and the wording that triggers on X and Twitter.
It records the owner's decisions of 2026-11-14.
This change is documentation only.

title: A test checks AI app results against official schemas
lines: A new test checks that the results of the AI app connector match the official MCP schemas, for two protocol versions.
This change adds a test only.
